content: 1. Doravirine metabolism is significantly influenced by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Adjustments to the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates should be made if clinically indicated, and therapy should be closely monitored. 2. St. John’s Wort is contraindicated as it decreases doravirine levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers is also contraindicated, as it may reduce doravirine plasma concentrations, leading to potential virologic failure and resistance development. 3. Stiripentol increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. Similarly, co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities, necessitating close monitoring. 4. Tazemetostat decreases doravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Telotristat ethyl is contraindicated for similar reasons, as it reduces doravirine levels and efficacy through CYP3A4 induction. 5. Tipranavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may lead to increased plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 6. Tucatinib significantly increases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes could result in severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose per product labeling and monitor closely. 7. Ublituximab decreases doravirine efficacy due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 8. Voriconazole increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. 9. Immune reconstitution syndrome has been reported in patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy, potentially causing inflammatory responses to latent or residual opportunistic infections (e.g., Mycobacterium avium, cytomegalovirus, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, or tuberculosis). This may require further evaluation and treatment. 10. Autoimmune disorders, such as Graves’ disease, polymyositis, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and autoimmune hepatitis, have been reported in the context of immune reconstitution. The onset of these conditions varies and may occur months after initiating treatment. 11. Healthcare providers are encouraged to register pregnant patients exposed to doravirine in the Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry (APR) by calling 1-800-258-4263. This registry monitors pregnancy outcomes in individuals exposed to doravirine during pregnancy. Currently, there is insufficient data to establish drug-associated risks to pregnancy outcomes. 12. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises against breastfeeding for HIV-infected women due to the potential risk of postnatal HIV transmission. It is unknown if doravirine is distributed in human breast milk. Women should be instructed not to breastfeed while taking this medication due to the risks of HIV transmission (in HIV-negative infants), viral resistance development (in HIV-positive infants), and adverse reactions in breastfed infants similar to those observed in adults. 13. Doravirine is generally acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 14. Doravirine is excreted unchanged in urine (6%) and minimally in feces/biliary excretion. It should be administered at a regularly scheduled time with or without food. If a dose is missed, it should be taken immediately unless it is almost time for the next dose. Patients should not take two doses simultaneously and should resume the next dose at the regularly scheduled time. 15. Store doravirine at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F). Keep the medication in its original bottle, tightly closed to protect from moisture, and do not remove desiccants. 16.
